correctness.rationale: For each omitted part, every opposite-side vertex has at most one missing neighbor, so three omissions cannot have singleton selected witnesses. The occupancy-two condition forces both indices into the deleted matching and disjointness from opposite omissions. For occupancy-one, the only remaining obstruction is a singleton selected opposite side at size three; subtraction yields the precise two exceptional terms. Nine disjoint cases prove the polynomial and all minimum cardinalities. A standalone direct witness simulation independently checks every subset for 130 graphs (407040 subsets), including exceptional cases. The quadratic coefficient ab+t(t-1) directly proves the polynomial separation/nonseparation corollary.

value.rationale: An exact all-cardinality super-domination enumerator for the natural three-parameter family K_{a,b} minus a matching isolates sharp stability thresholds: two missing edges allow three omitted vertices, four allow four, and the smallest crown graph is exceptional. Leading coefficients count all optimum choices; graph-modification studies and complete-bipartite scalar results do not supply these structural multiplicities. For fixed part sizes, the coefficient for two omitted vertices proves an exact separation boundary: t=0 and t=1 yield identical polynomials, but every t>=2 is distinguished.
